## intro
- minutes: "about 20 minutes"
- why: "Before you trust an answer, know three things about the session"
- can: "install Claude Code"
- can: "sign in"
- can: "start it in a repository"
- can: "tell which version, model and account a session is using"
- payoff: "tell which version, model and account a session is using"
- read: "[How Claude Code works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works): what happens between your question and its answer."

## steps

### W1 | Worked example step 1 of 7 | Install Claude Code
- tier: guided
- skill: install
- where: terminal
- beat: do
- verify: self
- done-label: it finished
- run: "curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash"
- win: "irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex"
- after: "When it finishes, open a new terminal window."
- say: Use that new window as your other terminal from now on.
- codespace: "In a Codespace on your copy, Claude Code is already installed: start at step 3."
- why: "Claude Code is a program you run in a terminal, inside a project folder."

### W2 | Worked example step 2 of 7 | Check the install
- tier: guided
- skill: install
- where: terminal
- beat: do
- verify: answer
- run: "claude --version"
- ask: What did it print?
- right: "a version number followed by `(Claude Code)`"
- stuck: "`claude` isn't found or isn't recognized"
- because: "If your shell says `claude` isn't found or isn't recognized, the install folder isn't on your `PATH` yet: fix it with [Troubleshoot installation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#command-not-found-claude-after-installation) before you go on."
- other: I saw something different
- codespace: "In a Codespace on your copy, Claude Code is already installed: start at step 3."

### W3 | Worked example step 3 of 7 | Save the version
- tier: guided
- skill: save-version
- where: terminal
- beat: do
- verify: check 0
- watching: .practice/version.txt
- evidence: .practice/version.txt
- goal: "Go to your practice copy and save that output for the check:"
- run: "cd <your practice copy>"
- run: "mkdir -p .practice"
- win: "New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .practice"
- tick: practice-dir
- run: "claude --version > .practice/version.txt"
- expect: "`.practice/version.txt` holds a line such as `X.Y.Z (Claude Code)`."
- why: "**the version**, because features and defaults change between releases;"

### W4 | Worked example step 4 of 7 | Start, sign in, trust
- tier: guided
- skill: start
- where: terminal
- beat: predict
- safety: trust-dialog
- note: "In a repository you haven't trusted yet, Claude Code also shows the workspace trust dialog, which asks whether you trust the folder"
- ask: Guess: which choice is highlighted at first?
- right: "**No, exit**"
- option: "**Yes, I trust this folder**"
- reveal: "**No, exit** is highlighted at first, and pressing Enter on it quits Claude Code."
- beat: do
- verify: self
- done-label: I'm signed in
- goal: "Start a session in the same folder:"
- run: "claude"
- note: "The first time, Claude Code asks you to sign in."
- do: "At the login prompt in the terminal, choose your account type; with a Claude subscription or Console account, you then finish in your browser."
- note: "With an API key or a cloud provider, follow the [Quickstart](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart) instead."
- hint: "If the browser shows a code instead of sending you back, paste it into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt"
- why: "It reads the files there and answers questions about them"
- beat: do
- where: claude
- verify: self
- done-label: I see the prompt
- do: "You made this copy, so press the Down arrow to choose **Yes, I trust this folder**, then press Enter."
- expect: "The header above the prompt then shows the version, the model and the folder."

### W5 | Worked example step 5 of 7 | Look at /status
- tier: guided
- skill: status
- where: claude
- beat: do
- verify: answer
- run: "/status"
- do: "Press `Esc` to close it"
- ask: Which three things did the Status tab list?
- wrong: "the version, the model and the folder"
- because: "The header above the prompt then shows the version, the model and the folder."
- right: "the version, the model and the account"
- wrong: "your session cost and plan usage limits"
- because: "Inside Claude Code, `/usage` shows your session cost and plan usage limits"
- other: I saw something different
- because: "Your version may be newer than the one at the top of this page"
- point: "rows such as **Login method** and **Email**"
- reveal: "The **Status** tab lists the version, the model and the account you signed in with (rows such as **Login method** and **Email**)."
- why: "**the model**, because models differ in what they can do;"
- why: "**the account**, because it decides which features and models you can use."

### W6 | Worked example step 6 of 7 | Ask about the code
- tier: guided
- skill: ask
- where: claude
- beat: do
- verify: none
- done-label: I asked both
- rule: "In this lesson, only ask questions"
- run: "what does this project do?"
- run: "which file parses linkcheck.json, and how do I run the tests?"
- note: "Claude reads files to answer."
- why: "A new session can edit most files and run most commands without asking you first"
- beat: ask
- ask: What did the answers name?
- right: `src/config.js` and `npm test`
- decoy: `src/links.js` and `npm run check`
- decoy: `src/cli.js` and `npm run linkcheck`
- other: Claude named something else
- reveal: "Your wording will differ, but the answers should name `src/config.js` and `npm test`."

- skill: exit

- beat: predict

- right: No, it won't ask again
- reveal-at: Y2

- verify: self

- beat: do

- why: "Even a question can lead Claude to run a command that writes files, such as running the tests to answer you"

## ladder

### `.practice/version.txt` holds the output of `claude --version`
- narrow "No `.practice/version.txt` yet": Which folder does the check name, and is it the folder where you ran the commands?
- narrow "is empty. Run `claude --version` on its own": What does `claude --version` print when you run it on its own?
- narrow "should hold a line such as": What does `cat .practice/version.txt` show?
- hint: "If the first item fails, run `claude --version` on its own: when it prints an error, fix it as Worked example step 2 describes; when it prints a version, save it again in the folder the check reads"
- bottom: "mkdir -p .practice"
- win: "New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .practice"
- bottom: "claude --version > .practice/version.txt"
